generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the broadleaf base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the broadleaf program gave as defaults until then.

traits.leaf_incision.note: DELTA, Acanthaceae (read 2026-10-17): blade undivided or dissected. Wikipedia: lobed only as an occasional margin form. Large genera (Justicia, Strobilanthes, Ruellia, Barleria) have undivided blades.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Wikipedia, Acanthaceae (read 2026-10-17): margins mostly smooth, at times toothed, lobed or spiny (Acanthus). DELTA, Acanthaceae (read 2026-10-17): margins entire, crenate, serrate or dentate. Order among the toothed states is my weighting (Strobilanthes, Ruellia often crenate-serrate).

traits.corolla_shape.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 331: flowers mostly monosymmetric with a long petal tube and an elaborate lower lip; Simpson p. 414 calls the corolla usually bilabiate.

traits.hypanthium.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 412: Simpson states the hypanthium is absent; flowers hypogynous.

traits.note: The Lucid key to the flowering plant families, with FloraBase and the Smithsonian's family text, as search results quote them (the pages themselves were not read): corolla sympetalous, usually 5-merous, mostly zygomorphic and commonly two-lipped; ovary superior on a nectar disc, of 2 fused carpels; stamens 4 (didynamous) or 2, on the corolla tube.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 325 Acanthaceae: herbs or climbers, rarely somewhat shrubby; leaves opposite; stipules absent; fruit a capsule, mostly springing open from the tip. APG adds the black mangroves (Avicennia), which also have opposite leaves and a capsule.

traits.rosette.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Acanthaceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Mendonciaceae, Nelsoniaceae, Thunbergiaceae: whether the leaves gather in rosettes (character 22), coded often a basal rosette, often no rosette. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.life_span.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Acanthaceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Mendonciaceae, Nelsoniaceae, Thunbergiaceae: the herbs' life form (character 21), coded often annual, often biennial, often perennial. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.leaf_division.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 412, 414, family Acanthaceae: leaf division simple; read as "simple".

traits.inflorescence.note: DELTA Acanthaceae (read 2026-10-17; ~2,400 spp, ~250 genera): flowers solitary or grouped in cymes, racemes or verticils; the ultimate units cymose in roughly three quarters of the coded genera, the rest racemose, dichasial cymes common. Genus weighting (approximate sizes, not read this session): Justicia (~700) and Dicliptera bear cymose clusters or cymose thyrses; Strobilanthes (~400) and Aphelandra carry dense bracteate spikes (added as sometimes); Ruellia and Barleria (~300 each) mix solitary flowers and cymes; Thunbergia flowers solitary. Re-ranks the earlier value, from plant-systematics-simpson, whose top states were tied.

traits.sexual_system.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 412, 414, family Acanthaceae: sexual system hermaphrodite; read as "hermaphrodite".

traits.bract_form.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 330, family Acanthaceae: bract form petaloid (showy), usually; read as {"petaloid": "usually"}.

traits.flowering_position.note: Ronse De Craene, Floral Diagrams (2010) p. 330, family Acanthaceae: flowering position terminal, usually; read as {"terminal": "usually"}.
